description: Phase 6 — Advanced features: local SSH on-device via Tauri russh backend, remote command execution via rstify webhooks, and command completion notifications

userStories.title: Tauri Rust backend SSH client (russh on-device)
userStories.description: As a mobile/desktop user on the same network as my servers, I want to SSH directly from my device without routing through the SvrCtlRS server, for lower latency and offline-from-server capability.
acceptanceCriteria: CONTEXT7 RESEARCH: Use Context7 MCP tool to query Tauri v2 docs for 'IPC commands Rust invoke frontend async channel'. Also query russh docs for 'client connect session channel exec shell'. Use latest patterns found.
Add russh as a dependency to ui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml
Create `ui/src-tauri/src/commands/ssh.rs` with Tauri IPC commands:
- `local_ssh_connect(hostname, port, username, auth_method)` — establishes SSH connection, returns session ID
- `local_ssh_execute(session_id, command)` — executes a command and returns output
- `local_ssh_shell_start(session_id, cols, rows)` — starts interactive shell with PTY
- `local_ssh_shell_input(session_id, data)` — sends input to the shell
- `local_ssh_shell_resize(session_id, cols, rows)` — resizes the PTY
- `local_ssh_disconnect(session_id)` — closes the connection
Manage active sessions in a HashMap<String, SshSession> behind a Mutex in Tauri state
Support SSH key auth (read from filesystem) and password auth
Register commands in lib.rs via `.invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![...])`
Desktop Tauri build still compiles: `cd ui && npx tauri build`
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
userStories.notes: This creates the Rust backend for local SSH. The frontend integration (US-003) connects this to the terminal UI. Tauri IPC commands are async Rust functions decorated with `#[tauri::command]`. They're called from JS via `invoke('command_name', { args })`. Session management: generate UUID for each connection, store in a Mutex<HashMap<String, SshSession>>. SshSession wraps a russh::client::Handle + Channel. For the shell, need a background task that reads from the channel and emits events to the frontend. Use Tauri's event system (`app.emit('ssh-output', data)`) for streaming output. Set env vars before building: JAVA_HOME, ANDROID_HOME, NDK_HOME.

userStories.title: Local SSH credential integration
userStories.description: As a user, I want local SSH connections to use my existing SvrCtlRS credentials and server profiles, so I don't need to re-enter connection details.
acceptanceCriteria: Create `ui/src-tauri/src/commands/credentials.rs` with a command to fetch credentials from the SvrCtlRS server API
When initiating a local SSH connection: look up the server's credential from the configured backend, or allow manual entry
Support reading SSH keys from the device filesystem (Tauri has fs access)
Support password auth with the credential's stored password
Add a 'Connect Locally' option in the command palette (alongside the existing 'Connect: servername' which goes through the server)
The 'Connect Locally' option only appears when isTauri() is true
`cd ui && npm run check` passes
`cd ui && npm run build` passes
userStories.notes: Local SSH needs credentials. Two approaches: (1) Fetch from the SvrCtlRS server API (requires server URL configured), (2) Store locally in Tauri secure storage. For Phase 6, use approach 1 — fetch from server API. The credential API at /api/v1/credentials already exists but redacts values in list mode. The get_credential endpoint also redacts. We may need a special endpoint or use the terminal's existing SSH connection logic as reference. Alternative: let the user specify the SSH key path manually in a dialog.

userStories.title: Frontend integration for local SSH terminal
userStories.description: As a user, I want to use the same xterm.js terminal UI for local SSH connections as I do for server-proxied connections.
acceptanceCriteria: CONTEXT7 RESEARCH: Use Context7 MCP tool to query Tauri v2 docs for 'invoke command frontend JavaScript async events listen emit'. Use latest patterns found.
Add a new connection mode to TerminalPane: 'local' (alongside existing 'pty' and 'cmd')
When mode is 'local': use Tauri invoke() instead of WebSocket to communicate with the SSH session
Terminal input: call `invoke('local_ssh_shell_input', { sessionId, data })` on xterm onData
Terminal output: listen for Tauri events `app.listen('ssh-output-{sessionId}', callback)` and write to xterm
Terminal resize: call `invoke('local_ssh_shell_resize', { sessionId, cols, rows })` on xterm onResize
Connection lifecycle: connect creates session via invoke, disconnect calls local_ssh_disconnect
Connection status updates work the same as WebSocket mode
`cd ui && npm run check` passes
`cd ui && npm run build` passes
userStories.notes: The key architectural difference: WebSocket mode streams data bidirectionally over a single connection. Local SSH mode uses Tauri IPC invoke() for input (client->rust) and Tauri events (rust->client) for output. The TerminalPane needs to detect the mode and use the appropriate communication channel. Import `invoke` and `listen` from '@tauri-apps/api/core' and '@tauri-apps/api/event'. The sessionId links input/output — generate it on connect and pass to all invoke calls.

userStories.title: Rstify webhook receiver for remote commands
userStories.description: As a user, I want to trigger pre-approved quick commands on my servers by sending a webhook from rstify or another system.
acceptanceCriteria: Create POST /api/v1/webhooks/execute endpoint that accepts a command execution request
Request format: `{ secret: string, command_name: string, server_name: string }` — identifies which quick command to run on which server
Security: validate `secret` against a configured webhook secret (stored in settings as `webhook.secret`)
Only execute commands that exist in the quick_commands table (allowlist enforcement)
Only execute on servers that exist and are enabled
Execute the command via the existing CMD mode SSH execution path
Send execution result (success/failure + output summary) back as a rstify notification
Add settings: `webhook.enabled` (boolean), `webhook.secret` (string)
Add migration seeding webhook settings
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
`cargo test --workspace` passes
userStories.notes: This is a simple webhook endpoint, NOT a full rstify integration client. External systems (CI/CD, monitoring, rstify's outgoing webhooks) POST to this endpoint to trigger pre-approved commands. Security is critical: (1) webhook.secret must match, (2) only commands in quick_commands table can be executed (no arbitrary commands), (3) the server must exist and be enabled. The execution path: look up quick command by name -> look up server by name -> execute via SSH (reuse terminal.rs execution logic) -> send result notification via rstify. Rate limiting would be nice but not required for Phase 6.

userStories.title: Command completion notifications
userStories.description: As a user running long commands in CMD mode, I want to get a push notification when the command completes.
acceptanceCriteria: When a CMD mode command completes (job_run finishes), check if notifications are enabled
If the command took longer than a configurable threshold (default 30 seconds), send a notification
Notification includes: command name/snippet, server name, exit code, duration
Add setting: `notification.cmd_completion_threshold_seconds` (default 30)
Only notify for CMD mode completions, not PTY sessions
Integrate into the existing terminal WebSocket handler (terminal.rs)
`cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
`cargo test --workspace` passes
userStories.notes: The terminal.rs CMD mode handler already executes commands and gets exit codes. After command completion, check the elapsed time. If > threshold, load notification config and send via NotificationClient. Keep it simple: just add a few lines after the command execution completes in the WebSocket handler. The notification message: 'Command completed on {server}: exit code {code} ({duration}s)'. Priority: 3 for success (exit 0), 7 for failure (non-zero exit).
